chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abdullah ibn Aasim, from Ali ibn Ismail al-Mithammi, from Rabie ibn Abdullah, from al-Fudayl who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about these things which the people play with, the dice and the chess, until I ended up to (mentioning) Al-Suddary (a game). So he (peace be upon him) said: 'If Allah were to Differentiate between the truth and the falsehood, in which of these two (categories) would (these games) fall into'. I said, 'With the falsehood'. He (peace be upon him) said: 'So what is it to you with the falsehood'.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on playing dice, chess, and Suddary in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Al-Fudayl bin Yakoub queries Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding the permissibility of games like backgammon (Nard), chess, and Suddary. The Imam employs a rhetorical syllogism, asking if these games are classified under 'truth' or 'falsehood' when God distinguishes between them; upon confirming they fall under falsehood, he concludes that their association with falsehood renders them impermissible. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential principle of deriving rulings from the essential nature of an act rather than just its mechanical components.
